In [[category theory]] and related fields of mathematics, an '''envelope''' is a construction that generalizes the operations of "exterior completion", like completion of a locally convex space, or [[Stone–Čech compactification]] of a topological space. A dual construction is called [[Refinement (category theory)|refinement]].

== Definition ==

Suppose <math>K</math> is a category, <math>X</math> an object in <math>K</math>, and <math>\Omega</math> and <math>\Phi</math> two classes of morphisms in <math>K</math>. The definition{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=42}} of an envelope of <math>X</math> in the class <math>\Omega</math> with respect to the class <math>\Phi</math> consists of two steps.
[[File:Extension-3.jpg|thumb|Extension.]]

* A morphism <math>\sigma:X\to X'</math> in <math>K</math> is called an ''extension of the object <math>X</math> in the class of morphisms <math>\Omega</math> with respect to the class of morphisms <math>\Phi</math>'', if <math>\sigma\in\Omega</math>, and for any morphism <math>\varphi:X\to B</math> from the class <math>\Phi</math> there exists a unique morphism <math>\varphi':X'\to B</math> in <math>K</math> such that <math>\varphi=\varphi'\circ\sigma</math>.
[[File:Envelope-3.jpg|thumb|Envelope.]]
 
* An extension <math>\rho:X\to E</math> of the object <math>X</math> in the class of morphisms <math>\Omega</math> with respect to the class of morphisms <math>\Phi</math> is called an ''envelope of <math>X</math> in <math>\Omega</math> with respect to <math>\Phi</math>'', if for any other extension <math>\sigma:X\to X'</math> (of <math>X</math> in <math>\Omega</math> with respect to <math>\Phi</math>) there is a unique morphism <math>\upsilon:X'\to E</math> in <math>K</math> such that <math>\rho=\upsilon\circ\sigma</math>. The object <math>E</math> is also called an ''envelope of <math>X</math> in <math>\Omega</math> with respect to <math>\Phi</math>''.
 
Notations:

<math>
\rho=\text{env}_{\Phi}^{\Omega}X, \qquad 
E=\text{Env}_{\Phi}^{\Omega}X.
</math>

In a special case when <math>\Omega</math> is a class of all morphisms whose ranges belong to a given class of objects <math>L</math> in <math>K</math> it is convenient to replace <math>\Omega</math> with <math>L</math> in the notations (and in the terms):
 
<math>
\rho=\text{env}_{\Phi}^L X, \qquad 
E=\text{Env}_{\Phi}^L X.
</math>

Similarly, if <math>\Phi</math> is a class of all morphisms whose ranges belong to a given class of objects <math>M</math> in <math>K</math> it is convenient to replace <math>\Phi</math> with <math>M</math> in the notations (and in the terms):
 
<math>
\rho=\text{env}_M^{\Omega} X, \qquad 
E=\text{Env}_M^{\Omega} X.
</math>

For example, one can speak about an ''envelope of <math>X</math> in the class of objects <math>L</math> with respect to the class of objects <math>M</math>'':

<math>
\rho=\text{env}_M^L X, \qquad 
E=\text{Env}_M^L X.
</math>

== Nets of epimorphisms and functoriality ==

Suppose that to each object <math>X\in\operatorname{Ob}({K})</math> in a category <math>{K}</math> it is assigned a subset <math>{\mathcal N}^X</math> in the class
<math>\operatorname{Epi}^X</math> of all epimorphisms of the category <math>{K}</math>, going from <math>X</math>, and the following three requirements are fulfilled:
* for each object <math>X</math> the set <math>{\mathcal N}^X</math> is non-empty and is directed to the left with respect to the pre-order inherited from <math>\operatorname{Epi}^X</math>
:: <math>\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in {\mathcal N}^X\quad \exists\rho\in{\mathcal N}^X\quad
\rho\to\sigma\ \& \ \rho\to\sigma',</math>
* for each object <math>X</math> the covariant system of morphisms generated by <math>{\mathcal N}^X</math>  
:: <math>\{\iota_\rho^\sigma;\ \rho,\sigma\in{\mathcal N}^X,\ \rho\to\sigma\}</math>
:has a colimit <math>\varprojlim {\mathcal N}^X</math> in <math>K</math>, called the ''local limit'' in <math>X</math>;
* for each morphism <math>\alpha:X\to Y</math> and for each element <math>\tau\in{\mathcal N}^Y</math> there are an element <math>\sigma\in{\mathcal N}^X</math> and a morphism <math>\alpha_\sigma^\tau:\operatorname{Cod}\sigma\to\operatorname{Cod}\tau</math><ref><math>\operatorname{Cod}\varphi</math> means the codomain of the morphism <math>\varphi</math>.</ref> such that 
:: <math>\tau\circ\alpha=\alpha_\sigma^\tau\circ\sigma.
</math>
Then the family of sets <math>{\mathcal N}=\{{\mathcal N}^X;\ X\in\operatorname{Ob}({K})\}</math> is called a ''net of epimorphisms'' in the category <math>{K}</math>.

'''Examples.'''
# For each [[locally convex topological vector space]] <math>X</math> and for each closed convex balanced neighbourhood of zero <math>U\subseteq X</math> let us consider its kernel <math>\operatorname{Ker}U=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\varepsilon\cdot U</math> and the quotient space <math>X/\operatorname{Ker}U</math> endowed with the normed topology with the unit ball <math>U+\operatorname{Ker}U</math>, and let <math>X/U=(X/\operatorname{Ker}U)^\blacktriangledown</math> be the completion of <math>X/\operatorname{Ker}U</math> (obviously, <math>X/U</math> is a [[Banach space]], and it is called the ''quotient Banach space'' of <math>X</math> by <math>U</math>). The system of natural mappings <math>X\to X/U</math> is a net of epimorphisms in the category <math>\text{LCS}</math> of locally convex topological vector spaces.  
# For each locally convex topological algebra <math>A</math> and for each ''submultiplicative'' closed convex balanced neighbourhood of zero <math>U\subseteq X</math>, 
:::: <math>U\cdot U\subseteq U</math>,
:: let us again consider its kernel <math>\operatorname{Ker}U=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\varepsilon\cdot U</math> and the quotient algebra <math>A/\operatorname{Ker}U</math> endowed with the normed topology with the unit ball <math>U+\operatorname{Ker}U</math>, and let <math>A/U=(A/\operatorname{Ker}U)^\blacktriangledown</math> be the completion of <math>A/\operatorname{Ker}U</math> (obviously, <math>A/U</math> is a [[Banach algebra]], and it is called the ''quotient Banach algebra'' of <math>X</math> by <math>U</math>). The system of natural mappings <math>A\to A/U</math> is a net of epimorphisms in the category <math>\text{LCS}</math> of locally convex topological algebras.  

'''Theorem.'''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|loc=Theorem 3.37}} ''Let <math>{\mathcal N}</math> be a net of epimorphisms in a category <math>{K}</math> that generates a class of morphisms <math>\varPhi</math> on the inside:''
:: <math>{\mathcal N} \subseteq \varPhi \subseteq \operatorname{Mor}({K}) \circ {\mathcal N}.
</math>
''Then for any class of epimorphisms <math>\varOmega</math> in <math>K</math>, which contains all local limits <math>\varprojlim {\mathcal N}^X</math>,''
:: <math>\{\varprojlim {\mathcal N}^X; \ X\in\operatorname{Ob}(K)\}\subseteq\varOmega\subseteq\operatorname{Epi}(K),</math>
''the following holds:''
:(i) ''for each object <math>X</math> in <math>{K}</math> the local limit <math>\varprojlim {\mathcal N}^X</math> is an envelope'' <math>\operatorname{env}_\varPhi^\varOmega X</math> in <math>\varOmega</math> with respect to <math>\varPhi</math>: 
:: <math>\varprojlim {\mathcal N}^X=\operatorname{env}_\varPhi^\varOmega X,</math>
:(ii) ''the envelope <math>\operatorname{Env}_\varPhi^\varOmega</math> can be defined as a functor.''

'''Theorem.'''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|loc=Theorem 3.38}} ''Let <math>{\mathcal N}</math> be a net of epimorphisms in a  category <math>{K}</math> that generates a class of morphisms <math>\varPhi</math> on the inside:''
:: <math>{\mathcal N} \subseteq \varPhi \subseteq \operatorname{Mor}({K}) \circ {\mathcal N}.
</math>
''Then for any monomorphically complementable class of epimorphisms <math>\varOmega</math> in <math>K</math> such that <math>K</math> is co-well-powered<ref>A category <math>K</math> is said to be ''co-well-powered in a class of morphisms'' <math>\varOmega</math>, if for each object <math>X</math> the category <math>\varOmega^X</math> of all morphisms in <math>\varOmega</math> going from <math>X</math> is skeletally small.</ref> in <math>\varOmega</math> the envelope <math>\operatorname{Env}_\varPhi^\varOmega</math> can be defined as a functor.''

'''Theorem.'''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|loc=Theorem 3.60}}
''Suppose a category <math>K</math> and a class of objects <math>L</math> have the following properties:''
:(i) <math>K</math> ''is [[cocomplete]],''
:(ii) <math>K</math> ''has [[nodal decomposition]],''
:(iii) <math>K</math> ''is co-well-powered in the class <math>\operatorname{Epi}</math>,''<ref>A category <math>K</math> is said to be ''co-well-powered in the class of epimorphisms'' <math>\operatorname{Epi}</math>, if for each object <math>X</math> the category <math>\operatorname{Epi}^X</math> of all morphisms in <math>\operatorname{Epi}</math> going from <math>X</math> is skeletally small.</ref>
:(iv) <math>\operatorname{Mor}(K,L)</math> ''goes from <math>K</math>:''
:: <math>\forall X\in\operatorname{Ob}(K)\quad \exists \varphi\in\operatorname{Mor}(K)\quad \operatorname{Dom}\varphi=X\quad\&\quad\operatorname{Cod}\varphi\in L</math>,
:(v) <math>L</math> ''differs morphisms on the outside: for any two different parallel morphisms <math>\alpha\ne\beta:X\to Y</math> there is a morphism <math>\varphi:Y\to Z\in L</math> such that <math>\varphi\circ\alpha\ne\varphi\circ\beta</math>,''
:(vi) <math>L</math> ''is closed with respect to passage to colimits,''
:(vii) <math>L</math> ''is closed with respect to passage from the codomain of a morphism to its [[nodal decomposition|nodal image]]: if <math>\operatorname{Cod}\alpha\in L</math>, then <math>\operatorname{Im}_\infty\alpha\in L</math>.''
''Then the envelope <math>\operatorname{Env}_L^L</math> can be defined as a functor.''

== Examples ==
In the following list all envelopes can be defined as functors.
: 1. The ''completion'' <math>X^\blacktriangledown</math> of a [[locally convex topological vector space]] <math>X</math> is an envelope of <math>X</math> in the category <math>\text{LCS}</math> of all locally convex spaces with respect to the class <math>\text{Ban}</math> of [[Banach space]]s:{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=50}} <math> X^\blacktriangledown=\text{Env}_{\text{Ban}}^{\text{LCS}}X</math>. Obviously, <math>X^\blacktriangledown</math> is the inverse limit of the quotient Banach spaces <math>X/U</math> (defined above):
::::<math>X^\blacktriangledown=\lim_{0\gets U}X/U.</math>
: 2. The [[Stone–Čech compactification]] <math>\beta:X\to\beta X</math> of a Tikhonov [[topological space]] <math>X</math> is an envelope of <math>X</math> in the category <math>\text{Tikh}</math> of all Tikhonov spaces in the class <math>\text{Com}</math> of [[compact space]]s with respect to the same class <math>\text{Com}</math>:{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=50}} <math> \beta X=\text{Env}_{\text{Com}}^{\text{Com}}X. </math>
: 3. The ''Arens-Michael envelope''{{sfn|Helemskii|1993|p=264}}{{sfn|Pirkovskii|2008}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2009|p=542}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2010|p=275}} <math>A^{\text{AM}}</math> of a locally convex topological  algebra <math>A</math> with a separately continuous multiplication is an envelope of <math>A</math> in the category <math>\text{TopAlg}</math> of all (locally convex) topological algebras (with separately continuous multiplications) in the class <math>\text{TopAlg}</math> with respect to the class <math>\text{Ban}</math> of Banach algebras: <math> A^{\text{AM}}= \text{Env}_{\text{Ban}}^{\text{TopAlg}}A </math>. The algebra <math>A^{\text{AM}}</math> is the inverse limit of the quotient Banach algebras <math>A/U</math> (defined above):
::::<math>A^{\text{AM}}=\lim_{0\gets U}A/U.</math>
: 4. The ''holomorphic envelope''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=170}} <math>\text{Env}_{\cal O} A</math> of a [[stereotype algebra]] <math>A</math> is an envelope of <math>A</math> in the category <math>\text{SteAlg}</math> of all stereotype algebras in the class <math>\text{DEpi}</math> of all ''dense'' epimorphisms<ref name=DEpi>A morphism (i.e. a continuous unital homomorphism) of stereotype algebras <math>\varphi:A\to B</math> is called dense if its set of values <math>\varphi(A)</math> is dense in <math>B</math>. </ref> in <math>\text{SteAlg}</math> with respect to the class <math>\text{Ban}</math> of all Banach algebras: <math> \text{Env}_{\cal O} A= \text{Env}_{\text{Ban}}^{\text{DEpi}}A. </math>
: 5. The ''smooth envelope''{{sfn|Akbarov|2017b|p=741}} <math>\text{Env}_{\cal E} A</math> of a [[stereotype algebra]] <math>A</math> is an envelope of <math>A</math> in the category <math>\text{InvSteAlg}</math> of all involutive stereotype algebras in the class <math>\text{DEpi}</math> of all ''dense'' epimorphisms<ref name=DEpi /> in <math>\text{InvSteAlg}</math> with respect to the class <math>\text{DiffMor}</math> of all differential homomorphisms into various C*-algebras with joined self-adjoined nilpotent elements: <math>\text{Env}_{\cal E} A= \text{Env}_{\text{DiffMor}}^{\text{DEpi}}A. </math>
: 6. The ''continuous envelope''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=179}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2017b|p=673}} <math>\text{Env}_{\cal C} A</math> of a [[stereotype algebra]] <math>A</math> is an envelope of <math>A</math> in the category <math>\text{InvSteAlg}</math> of all involutive stereotype algebras in the class <math>\text{DEpi}</math> of all ''dense'' epimorphisms<ref name=DEpi /> in <math>\text{InvSteAlg}</math> with respect to the class <math>\text{C}^*</math> of all C*-algebras: <math>\text{Env}_{\cal C} A= \text{Env}_{\text{C}^*}^{\text{DEpi}}A. </math>

== Applications ==

Envelopes appear as standard functors in various fields of mathematics. Apart from the examples given above, 

* the [[Gelfand transform]] <math> G_A:A\to C(\text{Spec} A)</math> of a commutative involutive [[stereotype algebra]] <math>A</math> is a continuous envelope of <math>A</math>;{{sfn|Akbarov|2016}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2013}} 

* for each [[locally compact abelian group]] <math>G</math> the [[Fourier transform]] <math> F_A:C^\star(G)\to C(\widehat{G})</math>  is a continuous envelope of the [[Group algebra of a topological group#Stereotype group algebras|stereotype group algebra]] <math>C^\star(G) </math> of measures with compact support on <math>G</math>.{{sfn|Akbarov|2016}} 

In [[abstract harmonic analysis]] the notion of envelope plays a key role in the generalizations of the [[Pontryagin  duality]] theory{{sfn|Akbarov|2017b}} to the classes of non-commutative groups: the holomorphic, the smooth and the continuous envelopes of [[stereotype algebra]]s (in the  examples given above) lead respectively to the constructions of the holomorphic, the smooth and the continuous dualities in ''big geometric disciplines'' – [[complex geometry]], [[differential geometry]], and [[topology]] – for certain classes of (not necessarily commutative) topological groups considered in these disciplines ([[affine algebraic group]]s, and some classes of [[Lie group]]s and Moore groups).{{sfn|Akbarov|2009}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2016}}{{sfn|Akbarov|2017b}}{{sfn|Kuznetsova|2013}}
